# Joseph and Aseneth Chapter 17 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 17:1 — new moon vs. first day of the month

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "on the new moon of the fourth month" | Literal noumēnia — lunar calendar term |
| LOGOS | "on the new moon of the fourth month" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "on the first day of the fourth month" | Explains the new moon reference |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** EMET and LOGOS agree: 'new moon.' This is a specific calendrical term (noumēnia) that should be preserved as such. PNEUMA's explanation is helpful but loses the lunar festival connotation. Adopted LOGOS.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 17:6 — our father our God — double title

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "our father our God" | Literal — unusual double address |
| LOGOS | "our father and our God" | Adds 'and' for clarity |
| PNEUMA | "our father and our God" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** The Greek has 'our father our God' asyndetically (without 'and'). LOGOS adds 'and' for natural English. EMET preserves the asyndeton, which is unusual. LOGOS adopted for readability while noting the asyndeton.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.
